You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. I need a refill on my spironolactone.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you with that refill. Before I get started, I need to verify your identity. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure thing, honey. January 19th, 1974.
[#14] AGENT: Thank you! Let me pull up your prescriptions. Great, Tess! Now let me look up your spironolactone prescription. Perfect! I found your spironolactone 25 milligram prescription with three refills remaining. I'll queue that refill for you at your home store, H-701. All set! Your spironolactone refill is queued and will be ready tomorrow, Friday, at ten in the morning at H-701. Anything else I can help you with today?
CALLER: Oh, one more thing - my knee's been bad, so I've been taking Advil, three or four a day, the 200s. Is that a problem?
[#17] AGENT: I'm glad you mentioned that, Tess. I can't advise on dosing or how medications work together—that's a question for your prescriber or our pharmacist. I'd recommend calling Dr. Rao or asking to speak with our pharmacist about whether that amount of Advil is okay with your current medications. Would you like me to have a pharmacist call you back about this?
CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. Yeah, please have the pharmacist call me back about it. I can hold off till I hear from them.
[#23] AGENT: Perfect, I'll flag that for our pharmacist to give you a call about the Advil and your medications. They'll reach out to you soon. Is there anything else I can help with today? Done! Our pharmacist will call you back about that. Have a great day, Tess!
CALLER: Sounds good, thanks so much honey. Bye now!
